title: Reaction norms for reproductive traits vary between lizard populations in response to local environments
content:
Abstract
Reproductive traits often vary across conspecific populations, but whether this variation follows geographic gradients or local ecological conditions remains unclear in many species. Here, we investigated female reproductive traits in four Eremias multiocellata and two Eremias przewalskii populations (including two sympatric localities: Minqin and Wulatehouqi) in northwestern China. For both species, females produced a single litter per breeding season. Postpartum body mass, litter size, and litter mass increased with female snout-vent length (SVL), and neonate mass and within-litter variability in neonate mass were SVL independent. After controlling for female SVL or postpartum body mass, inter-population differences existed in postpartum body mass, neonate mass, and relative litter mass but not in litter size or mass in each species. Sympatrically, E. przewalskii had larger maternal SVL, heavier neonates, greater postpartum body mass, and smaller litter size than E. multiocellata. Significant species × locality interactions indicated divergent local environmental effects. Within each species, Minqin females were larger and produced heavier neonates than Wulatehouqi females. Overall, reproductive traits exhibited population-level variation in a trait-specific pattern rather than conforming to simple geographic clines. These findings indicate that reproductive divergence in the two species is primarily shaped by locality-specific ecological conditions, instead of broad large-scale geographic trends.
